prompt: A photograph of a glazed ceramic piece on a wooden shelf, photographed as a real fired object. The piece is a small teapot whose handle is a modelled dragon and whose tail forms the spout, glazed in a running oxblood red over a stoneware body. The glaze has run and pooled thick and dark in every recess and pulled thin and pale over every raised edge, a fine web of crazing runs through the glaze surface, the unglazed foot ring shows raw grogged clay, there is one kiln kiss where the piece touched a shelf, and three small pinholes where the glaze bubbled. Shot on a 100mm macro at f8, soft light from a north window camera-left, the wet specular sheen of the glaze reading against the matte raw clay, natural colour.
medium_blurb: Kiln-fired earthenware under a running glaze.
